name: IEC open-circuit output, H-type (open emitter)
summary: Overlined diamond at an output: an open-emitter or open-source stage that can only drive a high level.
description: The H-type open-circuit output is drawn as a diamond with a line above it. It can supply a relatively low-impedance H level when on and is open when off, so it needs an external pull-down. TI's public overview notes it supports a positive-logic wired-OR connection.

Open-emitter outputs are typical of emitter-coupled logic and some line drivers. On a drawing the pull-down or termination must be shown, often to a negative or termination rail rather than to ground.
The qualifier does not give the termination value or rail. Those come from the logic family's application guidance and the device datasheet.
readingNotes: Overline above the diamond: drives high only.
Find the pull-down or termination on the net.
drawingChecklist: Draw the diamond with its overline next to the output.
Show the pull-down or termination and its rail.
Avoid joining H-type and L-type outputs on one net.
distinction: The L-type output has its line under the diamond and drives low only.
